For some reason I really hate SCP entries that have things spontaneously "appearing" and "vanishing" with no in-between state. Maybe have the box "fall apart" when the lid is removed (so it would be shaped like a + symbol) and the inside bottom of the box becomes the top of an elevator car that then rises from the floor and disgorges passengers and cargo. The elevator could have an inside larger than the outside so that furniture would fit inside. Then the elevator can sink back into the floor until the top of it is once again flush with the floor, where it could either repeat the process & bring more people/furnishings or can refuse with the panels of the box to become simple cardboard again. At this point the cardboard appears to fuse with the surface it has been placed on and becomes impossible to remove. After 5 hours the elevator returns on its own and carries away the party-goers & furnishings again & the box folds itself back up, but remains stuck to the floor until the lid is replaced.

Just a thought.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Except BAC is not based on a straight percentage. BAC is based on much smaller percentages. For example, a BAC of .10 is not ten percent of your blood is alcohol, it's one tenth of 1 percent.

So, a 1.8% of your blood being alcohol would actually be a BAC of 1.8, though the highest recorded BAC on record is about 1.4, it was not lethal. The idiot died from wounds sustained, not from his blood alcohol levels.

I couldn't find a quick reference to generally 'lethal' levels of BAC.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
"Autopsies reveal cause of death to be a combination of exhaustion and blood alcohol levels in excess of 1.8%."

Just a random technical fact — you state that the Blood alcohol content of the individuals exceeds 1.8% - Blood alcohol content is measured in % of blood by volume that is alcohol. Therefore, 1.0 is the highest BAC that is physically possible. 1.0 = 100% of the blood is alcohol. In this way, 1.8 means that 180% of an arbitrary volume exists, which defies physics. Or, we can interpret this as 1.8% of blood, by volume, is alcohol. This means that the BAC of the individuals would translate to a BAC of .018. This is well under the legal limit to drive in most states, and would technically be impossible to detect without specialized equipment.

Can you please change that sentence to clarify?

item.content:encoded:
Hmm. It does need just a tiny bit more punch. If you don't want to go the way of dialogue then you might want to bump that last paragraph into an addendum and don't bother redacting anything AND don't get stuck in the details. Expressing horror through dry scientific descriptions requires brevity and a sense of compassion-less distance from the material. And you might want to skip the hefty SCP-465-1 and SCP-465-2 designations for the box and its inhabitants for the overall piece, or at least designate them all up front in a bullet point list and then use easier names from there on out, like DJ, Barman and Guest or Party-goer or something

Here's what I'd write:

In approximately 10 percent of activations one or more "guests" become hysterical and attempt to flee the premises. Guests who manage to escape the immediate area surrounding SCP-465 or its activator vanish although they may be seen again on subsequent activations. Guests who are restrained or questioned have briefly complained about fatigue, loneliness and the whereabouts of their friends or families before falling into a catatonic state. No guest has ever been able to provide any significant identifying information in these circumstances or otherwise. Other guests will ignore this behavior or try to distract from it, while the DJ and Barman have been observed staring at these guests intently during such events.

item.content:encoded:
Of course he is being serious. My ideas shine out like a shaft of gold when all else is dark.

Ironic posturing aside, I seriously do recommend changing this from a party that tries to suck you in and into something that seems completely harmless and fun party in a box.

And then throw in at the end that all those people inside the box occasionally lose it like the way you have currently described, becoming hysterical and incoherent and begging to be freed or put out of their misery. That is a huge punch in the gut in terms of a tone shift. You go from "huh, okay. Weird item but not that special" to "Oh god. Who are they? How did they get IN there?"

And then most importantly, don't answer any of the questions that you raise. Let the reader freak out over all the implications. No test logs, no rescue attempts, nothing more than perhaps a recovery log about how someone had the box and used it for their own amusement until the party goers started freaking out. Maybe the original owner was brought up on kidnapping charges when people who visited his parties noticed the other guests were begging to be set free. You could even easily work in a MC&D angle there.
